items.text: Among adults with advanced solid tumours in the centre's eight clinics who meet a trigger criterion, do opt-out automatic referral triggers, compared with usual referral, increase days alive and out of hospital in the 90 days after trigger eligibility?
items.population: Adults with advanced solid tumours in the eight clinics who meet at least one trigger criterion
items.intervention: Automatic referral to specialist palliative care with oncologist opt-out
items.comparator: Usual referral at the oncologist's discretion
items.outcome: Days alive and out of hospital in the 90 days after the first trigger
items.time: 90 days after the first trigger; trial periods from the second quarter of 2027
items.setting: Regional cancer centre, eight disease-site clinics

items.text: Do triggers increase the proportion with a first specialist palliative care visit within 12 weeks, and how do they change the wait for a new palliative care appointment?
items.outcome: First visit within 12 weeks; days from referral to first appointment
items.time: 12 weeks after the first trigger; waiting time by month

finer: Feasible with routine data, existing clinics and the added nurse time; interesting to oncology, palliative care and families; novel for outpatient opt-out triggers; ethical subject to the board's decision on consent; relevant because referral timing is a known local problem.
summary: One primary PICO question and one process and balancing question.
